title: Topic Drill: Systems, Quadratics, Polynomials and Functions

items.stem: A neighborhood clinic fundraiser sold 40 dinner tickets for a total of $290. Adult tickets cost $8 and child tickets cost $5. How many child tickets were sold?
items.explanation: Let a + c = 40 and 8a + 5c = 290. Substituting a = 40 - c gives 320 - 8c + 5c = 290, so 3c = 30 and c = 10. The value 30 is the number of adult tickets, not child tickets. The value 40 is the total number of tickets. The value 58 divides 290 by 5 as though every ticket were a child ticket.

items.stem: A theater costume shop models two fabric charges with the system y = 2x - 3 and 3x + y = 17. Which ordered pair (x, y) is the solution of the system?
items.explanation: Substitute y = 2x - 3 into the second equation: 3x + 2x - 3 = 17, so 5x = 20 and x = 4, then y = 2(4) - 3 = 5. The pair (5, 4) swaps the coordinates. The pair (3, 3) fits only the first equation, since 9 + 3 is 12, not 17. The pair (2, 11) fits only the second equation, since 2(2) - 3 is 1, not 11.

items.stem: A community college lab technician combines two sensor readings that satisfy 3x + 2y = 18 and 5x - 2y = 14. What is the value of y?
items.explanation: Adding the equations cancels the y terms: 8x = 32, so x = 4. Then 3(4) + 2y = 18 gives 2y = 6 and y = 3. The value 4 is x, not y. The value 6 stops at 2y and forgets to divide by 2. The value 7 adds x and y together instead of reporting y alone.

items.stem: A hiking club compares two trail-fee rules, y = 3x + 4 and 6x - 2y = -8. How many solutions does this system have?
options: No solution, because the lines are parallel
Exactly one solution, because the equations are written differently
Infinitely many, because both equations describe the same line
Exactly two solutions, because each equation has two variables
items.explanation: Solve the second equation for y: -2y = -6x - 8, so y = 3x + 4, which is identical to the first equation. Identical lines share every point, so the system has infinitely many solutions. Calling the lines parallel ignores that their slopes and intercepts both match. Claiming one solution trusts the different look of the equations. A linear system can never have exactly two solutions.

items.stem: A coffee roaster sells one sample pack with 2 pounds of Ethiopian beans and 3 pounds of Colombian beans for $33, and another with 3 pounds of Ethiopian and 1 pound of Colombian for $32. What is the price per pound of the Ethiopian beans, in dollars?
items.explanation: Call the Ethiopian price e and the Colombian price k. From 3e + k = 32, k = 32 - 3e. Then 2e + 3(32 - 3e) = 33 gives -7e = -63, so e = 9 and k = 5. The value 5 is the Colombian price. The value 11 divides 33 by 3 as though the Ethiopian beans were free. The value 14 adds the two prices together.

items.stem: A bridge inspection firm offers two plans. Plan A costs 90 dollars plus 35 dollars per hour, and Plan B costs 40 dollars plus 45 dollars per hour. When the two plans cost the same, what is that cost in dollars?
items.explanation: Set 90 + 35h = 40 + 45h, so 50 = 10h and h = 5 hours. Plan A then costs 90 + 175 = 265, and Plan B costs 40 + 225 = 265. The value 130 adds the two fixed fees. The value 175 counts only the hourly part of Plan A. The value 225 counts only the hourly part of Plan B.

items.stem: A theater costume shop adds the yardage needed for two costume sets, (3x^2 + 5x - 7) and (2x^2 - 8x + 4). Which expression gives the total yardage?
items.explanation: Combine like terms: 3x^2 + 2x^2 = 5x^2, 5x - 8x = -3x, and -7 + 4 = -3. The expression 5x^4 adds the exponents, which is only done when multiplying. The expression with 13x subtracts the sign of -8x and gets 5 + 8. The expression ending in -11 subtracts 4 from -7 instead of adding it.

items.stem: A pottery studio shelf has an area modeled by (x + 4)(x - 7) square feet. Which expression is the product in standard form?
items.explanation: Multiply each pair: x times x is x^2, x times -7 is -7x, 4 times x is 4x, and 4 times -7 is -28. The middle terms combine to -3x, giving x^2 - 3x - 28. The expression x^2 - 28 multiplies only the first and last terms. The expression with +28 gets the constant sign wrong. The expression with +3x gets the sign of the middle term wrong.

items.stem: The load on one beam section during a bridge inspection is modeled by (2x - 3)(x^2 + 4x - 5). Which expression equals this product?
items.explanation: Distribute 2x: 2x^3 + 8x^2 - 10x. Distribute -3: -3x^2 - 12x + 15. Combining gives 2x^3 + 5x^2 - 22x + 15. The version ending in -15 gets the sign of -3 times -5 wrong. The version 2x^3 + 8x^2 - 10x - 3 multiplies only 2x across the trinomial. The version with +2x treats -3 times 4x as +12x.

items.stem: A pottery studio kiln shelf measures (x + 3) feet by (x + 5) feet. Which expression gives the area of the shelf in square feet?
items.explanation: Area is length times width, so (x + 3)(x + 5) = x^2 + 5x + 3x + 15 = x^2 + 8x + 15. The expression x^2 + 15 skips the middle terms. The expression x^2 + 15x + 8 swaps the 8 and the 15. The expression 4x + 16 is the perimeter, found by adding the sides, not the area.

items.stem: A bird count plot is a square whose side measures 3x - 2 meters. Which expression gives the area of the plot in square meters?
items.explanation: Area is (3x - 2)^2 = (3x - 2)(3x - 2) = 9x^2 - 6x - 6x + 4 = 9x^2 - 12x + 4. The expression 9x^2 + 4 squares each term and drops the middle term. The expression with -6x forgets the factor of 2 in the cross term. The expression ending in -4 forgets that -2 times -2 is positive.

items.stem: A community college lab models growth with the product (x^3 + 2x)(4x^2 - 1). After the product is multiplied out and simplified, what are its degree and leading coefficient?
items.explanation: Multiplying gives 4x^5 - x^3 + 8x^3 - 2x = 4x^5 + 7x^3 - 2x. The highest power is 5 and its coefficient is 4. Degree 6 multiplies the exponents 3 and 2 instead of adding them. Leading coefficient 8 comes from one partial product and is not the coefficient of the highest power. Degree 3 with coefficient 7 picks the combined middle term.

items.stem: A coffee roaster writes a cost formula for large wholesale bean orders as 12x^3 + 18x^2. Which choice is the completely factored form of the expression?
items.explanation: The greatest common factor of 12x^3 and 18x^2 is 6x^2, and dividing gives 2x and 3, so the result is 6x^2(2x + 3). The form 6x(2x^2 + 3x) is a true factoring but still has a common factor of x inside. The form 3x(4x^2 + 6x) still has a common factor of 2x inside. The form with 18 forgets to divide 18x^2 by 6x^2.

items.stem: A theater costume shop writes the area of a new cape pattern piece as x^2 + 9x + 20 square inches. Which is its factored form?
items.explanation: Find two numbers with product 20 and sum 9: 4 and 5 work, so the factors are (x + 4)(x + 5). The pair 2 and 10 has product 20 but sum 12. The pair 1 and 20 has product 20 but sum 21. The pair 9 and 20 uses the coefficients directly instead of searching for factors.

items.stem: A hiking trail crew models the cost of fencing a new overlook with the trinomial x^2 - 5x - 24. Which is its factored form?
items.explanation: Find two numbers with product -24 and sum -5: -8 and 3 work, giving (x - 8)(x + 3). The pair 8 and -3 has the correct product but a sum of +5. The pair -6 and 4 has product -24 but sum -2. The pair -12 and 2 has product -24 but sum -10.

items.stem: A pottery studio models the cost of a custom glaze batch with the binomial 49x^2 - 25. Which is its factored form?
items.explanation: Both terms are perfect squares, 49x^2 = (7x)^2 and 25 = 5^2, so the difference of squares gives (7x - 5)(7x + 5). The squared forms (7x - 5)^2 and (7x + 5)^2 would produce a middle term of -70x or +70x. The form with 25 forgets to take the square root of 25 and would expand to 49x^2 - 625.

items.stem: A bridge inspection report writes one stress term for a support beam as 2x^2 + 7x + 3. Which is its factored form?
items.explanation: Check (2x + 1)(x + 3): 2x^2 + 6x + x + 3 = 2x^2 + 7x + 3. The form (2x + 3)(x + 1) expands to 2x^2 + 5x + 3, so the middle term is wrong. The form (2x + 1)(x - 3) expands to 2x^2 - 5x - 3 and gets two signs wrong. The form (2x - 1)(x - 3) expands to 2x^2 - 7x + 3, which has the wrong middle sign.

items.stem: A bird count team writes a tally formula as 3x^2 - 15x + 18. Which is the completely factored form?
items.explanation: Pull out the common factor 3 to get 3(x^2 - 5x + 6), then factor the trinomial using numbers with product 6 and sum -5, namely -2 and -3. The form (3x - 6)(x - 3) is not complete, since 3x - 6 still has a factor of 3. The form with positive 2 and 3 has a middle term of +15x. The form with -1 and -6 has sum -7, giving -21x.

items.stem: A bird count plot has width w meters and length w + 3 meters, and its area is 40 square meters. What is the width of the plot, in meters?
items.explanation: Area gives w(w + 3) = 40, so w^2 + 3w - 40 = 0, which factors as (w + 8)(w - 5) = 0. The solutions are w = 5 and w = -8, and a width cannot be negative, so w = 5. The value -8 is the rejected negative root. The value 8 is the length, since 5 + 3 = 8. The value 40 is the area, not the width.

items.stem: A hiking trail sign is designed from the equation 3x^2 - 48 = 0. Which choice gives all of its solutions?
items.explanation: Add 48 and divide by 3 to get x^2 = 16. Taking square roots gives both x = 4 and x = -4. Listing x = 4 only forgets the negative root. The values 16 and -16 stop before taking the square root. The values 8 and -8 halve 16 instead of taking its square root.

items.stem: A clinic fundraiser models its profit target with 2x^2 - 7x + 3 = 0. Which choice gives all solutions found with the quadratic formula?
items.explanation: Here a = 2, b = -7 and c = 3. The discriminant is 49 - 24 = 25, so x = (7 plus or minus 5) / 4, which gives 3 and 1/2. The values 6 and 1 divide by 2 instead of 2a = 4. The values -3 and -1/2 use b instead of -b. The values 12 and 2 forget the denominator entirely.

items.stem: A community college lab student studies 3x^2 - 4x + 5 = 0. How many real solutions does the equation have?
options: Exactly one, because the discriminant is 0
Two, because the leading and constant coefficients are both positive
items.explanation: The discriminant is b^2 - 4(3)(5) = 16 - 60 = -44. A negative discriminant means there are no real solutions. The value 76 comes from adding 60 instead of subtracting it. A discriminant of 0 would need b^2 to equal 60, which it does not. Positive leading and constant coefficients do not guarantee solutions, because the size of b^2 relative to 4ac is what matters.

items.stem: A theater costume shop models its dye cost with 2x^2 - 5x - 3 = 0. What is the value of the discriminant?
items.explanation: The discriminant is b^2 - 4ac = (-5)^2 - 4(2)(-3) = 25 + 24 = 49. The value -49 changes the sign of the whole result. The value 1 subtracts 24, missing that c is negative. The value 37 uses 4 times c only, giving 25 + 12, and leaves out the coefficient a.

items.stem: A bridge inspection team knows that x^2 + kx + 9 = 0, with k greater than 0, has exactly one real solution. What is the value of k?
items.explanation: Exactly one real solution means the discriminant is zero: k^2 - 4(1)(9) = 0, so k^2 = 36 and k = 6, taking the positive value. The value 3 is the square root of the constant 9. The value 9 is the constant term itself. The value 36 is k^2, and the square root step was left out.

items.stem: A hiking trail overlook ramp follows y = x^2 - 8x + 5. What is the equation of its axis of symmetry?
items.explanation: The axis of symmetry is x = -b / (2a) = 8 / 2 = 4. The line x = -4 loses the sign of b. The line x = -8 uses b without dividing by 2a and also loses the sign. The line x = 13 adds 8 and the constant 5, which has no role in the axis.

items.stem: A pottery studio models the curve of a bowl rim with y = 2(x - 3)^2 + 7. What is the vertex of the parabola?
items.explanation: In y = a(x - h)^2 + k the vertex is (h, k), so here it is (3, 7). The point (-3, 7) flips the sign of h, though the factor is x minus 3. The point (7, 3) swaps the coordinates. The point (6, 7) multiplies h by the leading coefficient 2, which has no role in locating the vertex.

items.stem: At a clinic fundraiser, a foam disc launcher sends a disc to height h = -2t^2 + 12t + 1 feet after t seconds. What is the maximum height of the disc, in feet?
items.explanation: The peak occurs at t = -12 / (2 times -2) = 3 seconds. Then h = -2(9) + 12(3) + 1 = -18 + 36 + 1 = 19 feet. The value 1 is the starting height at t = 0. The value 3 is the time of the peak, not the height. The value 36 counts only 12 times 3 and leaves out the downward quadratic term.

items.stem: A coffee roaster models weekly cost with y = 3x^2 - 12x + 7. What is the minimum value of y?
items.explanation: The vertex is at x = 12 / 6 = 2, and y = 3(4) - 12(2) + 7 = 12 - 24 + 7 = -5. Because the leading coefficient is positive, this is a minimum. The value 2 is the x-coordinate of the vertex. The value 7 is the y-intercept. The value 12 is the size of the linear coefficient.

items.stem: A bridge arch crosses ground level at x = 2 and x = 10 on an inspection diagram. Which x value gives the line of symmetry of the arch?
items.explanation: The axis of symmetry lies halfway between the x-intercepts: (2 + 10) / 2 = 6. The value 4 is half the distance between the intercepts, not the midpoint. The value 8 is the full distance between them. The value 12 is the sum of the intercepts, with the division by 2 left out.

items.stem: A bird count team rewrites y = x^2 + 6x + 14 in vertex form by completing the square. Which equation is correct?
items.explanation: Half of 6 is 3, and (x + 3)^2 = x^2 + 6x + 9, so 14 - 9 = 5 must be added outside: y = (x + 3)^2 + 5. The form with +14 forgets to subtract the 9 that was added. The form with (x - 3) flips the sign inside the square. The form with (x + 6) uses b instead of b / 2.

items.stem: A theater costume shop models its weekly fabric use with the function g(x) = 3x^2 - x + 5, where x is a scaled input. What is g(-2)?
items.explanation: Substitute: g(-2) = 3(-2)^2 - (-2) + 5 = 3(4) + 2 + 5 = 19. The value -5 treats (-2)^2 as -4. The value 15 subtracts 2 instead of adding it, missing that minus a negative is positive. The value 43 squares the product 3 times -2, getting 36, instead of squaring only the -2.

items.stem: A community college lab models a signal reading with the function h(x) = -4x + 9, where x is the setting on a dial. What is h(-5)?
items.explanation: Replace x with -5: h(-5) = -4(-5) + 9 = 20 + 9 = 29. The value -29 gets both signs wrong. The value -11 evaluates h(5) and ignores the negative input. The value 11 gets the product right as 20 but subtracts 9 instead of adding it.

items.stem: A coffee roaster models weekly profit in hundreds of dollars with f(x) = 3x - 5. For what input a is f(a) equal to 19?
items.explanation: Set 3a - 5 = 19, add 5 to get 3a = 24, and divide by 3 to get a = 8. The value 14 subtracts 5 from 19 and stops. The value 24 adds 5 correctly but stops before dividing by 3. The value 52 evaluates f(19) instead of solving f(a) = 19.

items.stem: A bridge inspection gauge follows f(x) = kx - 4, and f(4) = 20. What is the value of k?
items.explanation: Substitute: 4k - 4 = 20, so 4k = 24 and k = 6. The value 5 divides 20 by 4 and ignores the -4. The value 16 subtracts 4 from 20 instead of adding it. The value 24 adds correctly but stops before dividing by 4.

items.stem: A hiking club defines f(x) = x^2 + 1 to compute trail difficulty scores from a base rating. Which expression equals f(a + 2)?
items.explanation: Replace x with a + 2: (a + 2)^2 + 1 = a^2 + 4a + 4 + 1 = a^2 + 4a + 5. The expression a^2 + 3 computes f(a) + 2 instead. The expression a^2 + 5 squares each term of the binomial separately and loses 4a. The expression a^2 + 4a + 4 squares correctly but forgets the +1.

items.stem: A coffee roaster uses C(n) = 12n + 150 for the dollar cost of n batches. What does the statement C(25) = 450 mean?
options: Each of the first 25 batches costs $450
The cost rises $25 for every 450 batches
items.explanation: The input of C is the number of batches and the output is dollars, so C(25) = 450 says 25 batches cost $450. Check: 12(25) + 150 = 450. Reversing input and output claims 450 batches cost $25. Saying each batch costs $450 confuses the total with a unit price. Saying the cost rises $25 per 450 batches mixes up the rate of change.

items.stem: A bridge inspection program uses the rule f(x) = sqrt(x - 4), where x is a sensor reading. Which description gives the domain of f?
options: All real numbers greater than or equal to 4
All real numbers less than or equal to 4
items.explanation: The square root of a negative number is not real, so x - 4 must be at least 0, which means x is 4 or more. Excluding 4 itself is wrong because sqrt(0) = 0 is defined. Excluding only 4 allows readings below 4, which give negative radicands. Choosing values at most 4 reverses the inequality.

items.stem: A pottery studio models glaze thickness with y = x^2 + 3. Which description gives the range of the function?
options: All real numbers less than or equal to 3
All real numbers greater than or equal to 0
All real numbers greater than or equal to 3
items.explanation: Because x^2 is never negative, its smallest value is 0, so y is never below 0 + 3 = 3. Every output from 3 upward is reached. Saying all real numbers ignores the minimum. Saying outputs are at most 3 reverses the direction of the parabola. Saying outputs start at 0 forgets that the +3 shifts the whole graph up.

items.stem: A theater costume shop models stage lighting with f(x) = 1 / (x + 5). Which description gives the domain of f?
items.explanation: Division by zero is undefined, and x + 5 equals 0 when x = -5, so only -5 is excluded. Excluding 5 solves x - 5 = 0 by mistake. Requiring x greater than -5 treats the denominator like a square root. Allowing all real numbers ignores the zero denominator.

items.stem: A hiker’s elevation is modeled by E(t) = 300 + 250t meters, where t is the hours on the trail and 0 <= t <= 4. Which description gives the range of E?
options: All elevations from 0 meters to 1,300 meters
All elevations from 300 meters to 1,300 meters
All elevations of 300 meters or more
items.explanation: The range lists output values: E(0) = 300 and E(4) = 300 + 1,000 = 1,300, and the line is increasing, so every elevation from 300 to 1,300 occurs. Listing 0 to 4 hours names the domain. Starting at 0 meters ignores the 300-meter starting point. Allowing 300 or more ignores the four-hour limit.

items.stem: A coffee roaster models heat loss with y = -x^2 + 6. Which description gives the range of the function?
options: All real numbers greater than or equal to 6
All real numbers less than or equal to 6
All real numbers less than or equal to 0
items.explanation: The term -x^2 is never positive, so its largest value is 0 and y never exceeds 6. The outputs run from 6 downward without limit. Choosing 6 or more reverses the direction because the parabola opens downward. Choosing all real numbers ignores the maximum of 6. Choosing at most 0 forgets the +6 that lifts the vertex.

items.stem: A bird count records (hour, species) pairs: (1, 4), (2, 7), (3, 4), (5, 9). Which list gives the range of this relation?
items.explanation: The range is the set of distinct outputs, which are the second numbers: 4, 7 and 9, with 4 listed once. The list 1, 2, 3 and 5 gives the domain. The list 4, 7, 4 and 9 repeats 4, though a set lists each value only once. The interval from 4 to 9 treats the relation as continuous, but only three outputs occur.

items.stem: A coffee roaster records batches and kilograms as (0, 2), (1, 5), (2, 8), (3, 11). What type of growth does the table show, and why?
options: Linear, because each step adds the same 3
Quadratic, because the outputs get larger
Linear, because the first output is 2
Quadratic, because the second differences are 3
items.explanation: The outputs rise by 3, 3 and 3, a constant first difference, which is linear growth. Growing larger does not make a table quadratic, since a line also grows. The starting value of 2 does not decide the type. The second differences are all 0, not 3, because the first differences never change.

items.stem: A pottery studio records visits and clay used as (0, 1), (1, 3), (2, 7), (3, 13). Which statement best describes the growth?
options: Linear, because the outputs always increase
Quadratic, because the first differences 2, 4 and 6 grow by a constant 2
Linear, because the first output is 1
Quadratic, because the outputs are all odd
items.explanation: The first differences are 2, 4 and 6, which are not constant, but the second differences are 2 and 2, a constant. A constant second difference signals a quadratic. Steady increase alone does not make growth linear. The starting value is irrelevant. Oddness of the outputs has no connection to the type of growth.

items.stem: At a clinic fundraiser, Pledge A raises 20n + 10 dollars after n weeks and Pledge B raises n^2 dollars. Among the weeks 10, 20, 30 and 40, at which is Pledge B first above Pledge A?
items.explanation: At week 10, A is 210 and B is 100. At week 20, A is 410 and B is 400, still just below. At week 30, A is 610 and B is 900, so B first exceeds A there. Week 10 reads the early lead for B. Week 20 rounds the near tie in B’s favor. Week 40 is also true, but it is not the first week.

items.stem: A coffee roaster’s output is L(n) = 6n + 4 for one machine and Q(n) = n^2 + 1 for another. How much greater is Q(8) than L(8)?
items.explanation: Compute L(8) = 48 + 4 = 52 and Q(8) = 64 + 1 = 65, so the difference is 65 - 52 = 13. The value -13 subtracts in the wrong order. The value 35 treats n^2 as 2n, making Q(8) = 17. The value 117 adds the two outputs instead of finding the difference.

items.stem: A bridge inspection model gives crack depth d(x) = x^2 millimeters after x months. What is the average rate of change of d from month 3 to month 5, in millimeters per month?
items.explanation: Average rate is (d(5) - d(3)) / (5 - 3) = (25 - 9) / 2 = 8. The value 10 is 2 times 5, the instantaneous rate at month 5, not the average over the interval. The value 16 finds the change in depth and forgets to divide by 2. The value 34 adds 25 and 9 instead of subtracting.

items.stem: A coffee roaster’s warehouse stock follows s(t) = 50t for one product and r(t) = t^2 + 100 for another, where t is the number of weeks. Which statement about long-term growth is correct?
options: The linear stays larger for all weeks, because 50 is bigger than 1
They stay equal, because both grow every week
The quadratic eventually exceeds the linear one, because its rate of increase keeps growing
The linear exceeds the quadratic after week 100, because 100 is the larger constant
items.explanation: A linear function adds a fixed amount each week, while a quadratic adds more each week, so it eventually overtakes any line. Here t^2 + 100 passes 50t after about week 48. Comparing only the coefficients 50 and 1 ignores the squared variable. Growing every week does not make two functions equal. The constant 100 has no effect on the long-term comparison.

items.stem: A community college lab student multiplies the two monomials (2x^3)(5x^4) while simplifying a growth model. Which expression is the product?
items.explanation: Multiply the coefficients, 2 times 5 = 10, and add the exponents, 3 + 4 = 7, giving 10x^7. The expression 7x^7 adds the coefficients, 2 + 5, instead of multiplying them. The expression 10x^12 multiplies the exponents. The expression 10x^3 subtracts the exponents, a rule that belongs to division.

items.stem: A theater costume shop scales a pattern piece using the power expression (3x^2)^3 in its sizing sheet. Which expression is equivalent?
items.explanation: A power of a product raises every factor to the power: 3^3 = 27 and (x^2)^3 = x^6, giving 27x^6. The expression 9x^6 multiplies 3 by 3 instead of cubing it. The expression 27x^5 adds the exponents 2 and 3. The expression 3x^6 leaves the coefficient unchanged.

items.stem: A coffee roaster simplifies the ratio 24x^9 / 6x^3 when comparing two bean storage models for the warehouse. Which expression is the quotient?
items.explanation: Divide the coefficients, 24 / 6 = 4, and subtract the exponents, 9 - 3 = 6, to get 4x^6. The expression 4x^3 divides the exponents, 9 / 3, which is not a rule for quotients. The expression 18x^6 subtracts the coefficients. The expression 4x^12 adds the exponents.

items.stem: A bird count spreadsheet writes one growth term as 5x^-2, and the volunteers want a form with positive exponents. Which expression is equivalent?
items.explanation: A negative exponent moves only its own base to the denominator, so x^-2 = 1 / x^2 and 5x^-2 = 5 / x^2. The expression 1 / (5x^2) wrongly moves the coefficient too. The expression 5x^2 ignores the negative sign of the exponent. The expression -5x^2 treats a negative exponent as a negative number.

items.stem: A community college lab student evaluates a dilution expression written as 3^0 + 2^3 times 2^-1. What is its value?
items.explanation: Any nonzero base to the power 0 equals 1, and 2^3 times 2^-1 = 2^2 = 4, so the sum is 1 + 4 = 5. The value 4 treats 3^0 as 0. The value 7 treats 3^0 as 3. The value -15 treats 2^-1 as -2, giving 8 times -2 = -16, then adds 1.

items.stem: A pottery studio simplifies the glaze mixing ratio (2x^3 y^2)^2 / (4x^2 y) for a new kiln schedule. Which expression is equivalent?
items.explanation: The numerator is 4x^6 y^4. Dividing by 4x^2 y cancels the 4 and subtracts exponents: x^(6 - 2) y^(4 - 1) = x^4 y^3. The expression x^4 y^2 subtracts 2 from the y exponent. The expression x^3 y^3 divides 6 by 2. The expression x^8 y^3 adds the x exponents.

items.stem: A bridge inspection index uses the function g(x) = 3x - 5 first and then squares the result with f(x) = x^2. What is f(g(4))?
items.explanation: Work inside out: g(4) = 12 - 5 = 7, then f(7) = 49. The value 7 stops after the inner function. The value 14 doubles 7 instead of squaring it. The value 43 finds g(f(4)) = g(16) = 43, reversing the order of the functions.

items.stem: Let f(x) = x + 4 and g(x) = x^2 be two rules a pottery studio uses to scale orders. Which expression equals g(f(x))?
items.explanation: Replace the input of g with f(x): g(f(x)) = (x + 4)^2 = x^2 + 8x + 16. The expression x^2 + 4 is f(g(x)), the reverse order. The expression x^2 + 16 squares each term and drops the middle term. The expression x^2 + 4x + 16 forgets the factor of 2 in the cross term.

items.stem: A theater costume shop uses f(n) = yards of fabric for n capes, with f(1) = 4, f(2) = 7 and f(3) = 10. A cost rule g gives g(4) = 12, g(7) = 20 and g(10) = 29 dollars. What is g(f(2))?
items.explanation: First f(2) = 7 yards, then g(7) = 20 dollars, so the cost of two capes is 20. The value 7 is the inner result only. The value 12 uses f(1) = 4 and gives g(4). The value 29 uses f(3) = 10 and gives g(10), the cost of three capes.

items.stem: A coffee roaster uses f(x) = 2x - 1 and g(x) = x + 3. For what value of x is f(g(x)) = 11?
items.explanation: Compose: f(g(x)) = 2(x + 3) - 1 = 2x + 5. Setting 2x + 5 = 11 gives x = 3. The value 2 turns the -1 into +1 after distributing. The value 6 stops at 2x = 6 without dividing by 2. The value 8 subtracts 3 from 11 as if g were applied outside.

items.stem: A hiking club defines f(x) = x^2 - 3 and g(x) = 2x + 1 for scoring trail routes. Which expression equals f(g(x))?
items.explanation: Substitute g(x) into f: (2x + 1)^2 - 3 = 4x^2 + 4x + 1 - 3 = 4x^2 + 4x - 2. The expression 4x^2 - 2 drops the middle term when squaring. The expression 2x^2 - 5 is g(f(x)), the reverse order. The expression 4x^2 + 2x - 2 forgets the factor of 2 in the cross term.

items.stem: A pottery studio uses p(n) = 12n for pounds of clay needed for n students and c(p) = 2p + 15 for the dollar cost of p pounds. Which expression gives the cost in terms of n?
items.explanation: Substitute p(n) into c: c(p(n)) = 2(12n) + 15 = 24n + 15. The expression 24n + 180 multiplies the 15 by 12 as well. The expression 14n + 15 adds 12n and 2n instead of multiplying them. The expression 2n + 27 adds 12 to the 15 instead of substituting 12n for p.
